brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: One keyhole hanger on the wall-side face of each storey: accessory:0#0,0#2 and accessory:1#0,0#2. Both are on the same flat face, so they sit flush against the wall. I can't confirm the plastic is strong enough to hold the rack's weight.

6 hook plates with two hooks each (12 hooks), on the front and angled front faces of both storeys: accessory:0#0,0#0/4/5 and accessory:1#0,0#0/4/5. I couldn't stage hand tools on them because the catalog only lets gaffer tape, a cable coil or goggles hang on a hook.
A two-storey hex column (piece:0,0,0 and piece:0,0,1), joints locked. The collision check came back clear.

finish.summary: I built a wall tool rack from two hex cells stacked into a column at cell 0,0 (levels 0 and 1). It has 2 keyhole hangers and 6 hook plates, which give 12 hooks, for 17 parts in total. Both keyhole hangers are on the face that goes against the wall. The hook plates are on the front face and the two angled faces next to it on each storey. I ran the joint-locking step. The step that caps open faces added no caps, and 4 side faces are still open, so the check reports them as info only. The collision check came back clear. To show the rack in use I hung gaffer tape and a cable coil on the upper hooks. The tool catalog only lets those props hang on hooks, so I couldn't show actual hand tools hanging there. The configurator wouldn't let me hang props on the lower hooks because the build sits on the bench in the view: a cable coil would have hung 35 mm into it. Once the rack is on the wall, those hooks hang free.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
